# Hybrid and Remote Work Policy — Lumen Ridge Software, Inc.

## Purpose and scope
This Policy gives us one clear rule for where and how we work. It applies to all 340 employees in California, Illinois, Texas, New York, and Washington.

It replaces Memo A (2023), Memo B (2024), and Memo C (2024). If there is a conflict with an old memo or verbal instruction, this Policy controls.

## Work arrangements (onsite / hybrid / remote, and who falls into which)
Your arrangement is based on your home address and your role:

* **Hybrid:** Your primary residence is within 50 miles of our San Jose, Chicago, or Austin office. Most employees in California, Illinois, and Texas are hybrid.
* **Remote:** Your primary residence is more than 50 miles from an office. All employees in New York and Washington are remote, as we have no office there.
* **Onsite:** Only roles specifically designated as onsite in the offer letter. Very few roles are onsite.

People will confirm your arrangement in writing. Moving does not automatically change it — see Changing your home state.

## Office attendance
Hybrid employees **must** work in their assigned office Tuesday through Thursday, unless on approved leave or approved alternate location work.

Mondays and Fridays are flexible: you may work from home if your job allows it and your manager approves. Remote employees are not required to come in, except for team gatherings with at least 14 days' notice. We will pay travel as required by this Policy and law.

Core collaboration hours are 10am-3pm in your office time zone.

## Working from another location (in the US and abroad)
**In the US:** You may work from another US location for up to 20 workdays (4 weeks) per calendar year, with prior manager approval. You must be available, keep a secure workspace, and continue to meet attendance and timekeeping rules. This does not change your home state.

**Outside the US:** You must not work abroad without prior written approval from People and Legal, requested at least 60 days in advance. Even with approval, work abroad is limited to Canada and the UK, where we have an entity or employer-of-record, and counts toward your 20-day limit. We cannot approve other countries at this time due to immigration, tax-withholding, and permanent-establishment risk.

Unapproved work from abroad is prohibited.

## Changing your home state
You must live and work in your state of hire. If you want to move states, you must get People team approval at least 60 days in advance.

We currently operate only in CA, IL, TX, NY, and WA. A move to another state, or a move that changes your hybrid/remote status, is not guaranteed and may require a role change or separation.

## Equipment and expense reimbursement (with state-specific rules)
We provide a laptop and required peripherals. You must use approved security tools and return equipment on exit.

**Everyone** in hybrid or remote work receives a $50/month home-office stipend via payroll. It replaces Memo C's phone/internet rule.

State-specific rules:

* **California:** If your actual necessary home-office expenses exceed $50 in a month, submit receipts via the expense system within 30 days. We will reimburse the verified excess, as required by Labor Code §2802.
* **Illinois:** If your actual necessary expenses exceed $50, submit receipts and a business purpose within 30 days. We will reimburse the verified excess. If you do not follow this written procedure, we are not liable for that claim.
* **Texas, New York, Washington:** The $50 stipend applies. Additional reimbursement only if pre-approved in writing.

No reimbursement without required receipts where receipts are required.

## Hours, timekeeping and non-exempt employees
This applies to everyone, especially our 58 non-exempt employees.

You must record **all** hours worked, including booting up, logging into the VPN and other required systems, troubleshooting required logins, and any work before or after your scheduled shift. That time is paid work time.

No off-clock work. Do not work without recording time, and managers must not ask you to. Overtime must be pre-approved, but we will pay all overtime worked. Meal and rest breaks will follow the law of your work state.

## Exceptions and accommodations
If you need an exception for disability, medical condition, pregnancy, or religion, contact the People team to request a reasonable accommodation. We will engage in an interactive process. Other schedule exceptions require manager and People approval.

## Policy owner and effective date
Owner: Head of People. Effective: November 1, 2026. We will review annually. Questions: People team.

### Summary by state

| State | Typical arrangement | Office rule | Expense rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| California (120) | Hybrid if <50 mi from San Jose, else Remote | Tue-Thu if hybrid | $50 + claim excess with receipts |
| Illinois (70) | Hybrid if <50 mi from Chicago, else Remote | Tue-Thu if hybrid | $50 + claim excess with receipts within 30 days |
| Texas (85) | Hybrid if <50 mi from Austin, else Remote | Tue-Thu if hybrid | $50 stipend |
| New York (40) | Remote | No office; gatherings only | $50 stipend |
| Washington (25) | Remote | No office; gatherings only | $50 stipend |

---
### Note to CEO — decisions needed (178 words)

I kept your 3-day Tue-Thu model for those within 50 miles and remote for others, replacing Memo B's 2-day rule. I departed from three instructions to avoid legal risk:

1. **$50 flat with no receipts:** California requires full reimbursement of necessary expenses; a flat amount is only lawful if staff can claim the shortfall. Illinois also requires reimbursement of necessary expenses under a written policy. I kept $50 for all, plus a receipt-based top-up for CA/IL.

2. **Work from anywhere abroad:** Counsel warns even short stays create immigration, tax, and permanent-establishment risk. I limited abroad work to Canada and the UK with 60-day People + Legal pre-approval, counting toward the 4-week US limit. Unrestricted abroad work is prohibited.

3. **Unpaid boot-up/VPN time:** Federal guidance treats required boot-up/log-in as compensable. I require all non-exempt staff to record and be paid for it, and ban off-clock work.

**Decision needed:** Please approve (a) the CA/IL top-up process and (b) the Canada/UK-only abroad limit. If you want more abroad countries, we need Legal to add an employer-of-record first.
